requirement_text.REQ-054: Port src/engine/snapshot_writer.zig (348 lines -- R-Co's ISS-601, design artefact src/design/iss601_state_snapshots.md) as Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter, plus its instance_state_snapshots migration and Ecto.Schema module (schema-per-tenant per REQ-022, same as every other table this stage adds). THIS REQUIREMENT EXTENDS REQ-053's already-shipped reconstruct path -- it is not a standalone module. REQ-053 builds full-log replay from sequence 1; this requirement adds the snapshot table, the writer, and the replay-source selection that lets that same reconstruct function start from the latest snapshot instead. The deliverable is therefore a modification of REQ-053's function plus new supporting code, and the correctness bar below is that both paths agree. Purpose: reconstruction (REQ-053) replaying the FULL event log from sequence 1 is O(events) and gets slower forever. A periodic snapshot of the InstanceState as a jsonb blob lets reconstruction replay only the events SINCE the latest snapshot. - take_snapshot/N: serialises REQ-044's InstanceState (status, tokens, variables, pending task nodes, error_detail) plus the sequence_number it is current as of, into an instance_state_snapshots row. - maybe_take_snapshot/N: the cadence check -- snapshot every N events, default 1000 per snapshot_writer.zig's DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL. Called after event appends and on instance completion. - REQ-053's replay-source selection: given a latest snapshot at sequence S, replay only events with sequence_number > S on top of the deserialised snapshot state, versus replaying from 1 when no snapshot exists (reconstruction.zig's determineReplaySourceForSnapshot()). This requirement extends REQ-053's reconstruct path to use snapshots when present -- and the correctness bar is that BOTH paths produce the identical state, since a snapshot that diverges from full replay is worse than no snapshot at all. - This table is NOT the same thing as REQ-027/REQ-033's instance_definition_snapshots (the immutable PD-08 DEFINITION graph bound to an instance at start). These are periodic EXECUTION STATE snapshots, mutable in the sense that new rows accumulate over an instance's life. Say so explicitly in the moduledoc -- the two names are one word apart and confusing them would be a silent data-model error. OPEN QUESTION (flag, do not silently resolve): where the events-since-last-snapshot counter lives. instance_projections.last_event_seq (REQ-023) already tracks the latest sequence per instance, which makes a pure row-based cadence check possible with no in-memory counter at all; R-Co's own SnapshotWriter is a struct holding a pool handle. If REQ-045 resolved to supervised processes, an in-process counter is available but is exactly the kind of state stage-3-instance-engine.md's second Early finding warns is NOT automatically worth a process. Leave the choice to CODE-DESIGNER, citing that finding and REQ-045's resolution.

task.description:
Implement lib/letflow/design/req054-instance-state-snapshots.md: the instance_state_snapshots migration (schema-per-tenant, no tenant_id per Decision 0006 D2), its Ecto.Schema module, Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter (take_snapshot/4, maybe_take_snapshot/4, latest_snapshot/2), and the modification to Reconstruction.replay/3 (or reconstruct_instance/2, per the design doc's exact naming) to add select_replay_source/2 and widen read_full_log to accept a min_sequence_number filter.

REWORK ITERATION 1: REVIEWER (step-02d) FAILed this implementation -- SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4 exists but is never called from lib/letflow/engine.ex. grep -rn maybe_take_snapshot across lib/ and test/ finds zero call sites outside its own definition. The design doc (lib/letflow/design/req054-instance-state-snapshots.md §4.2, §8) explicitly requires wiring at Engine's event-append points and instance completion, naming create/2, complete_task/3, and ExecutionError.append_multi/3 by name. Wire maybe_take_snapshot/4 into lib/letflow/engine.ex's create/2 (~line 211), complete_task/3's completion paths (~lines 1313-1524), and the ExecutionError.append_multi/3 call sites (~lines 1263, 1948 via set_instance_error/2) -- or explicitly justify a narrower subset in your handoff rather than shipping partial wiring silently again. Re-run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix ecto.migrate, mix format --check-formatted, and the full mix test suite after wiring; quote real output.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains an instance_state_snapshots migration, schema-per-tenant per REQ-022, applying cleanly against a provisioned tenant schema
take_snapshot writes a row whose deserialised state equals the InstanceState passed in, round-tripped field-for-field including tokens and variables
maybe_take_snapshot writes no row before the interval is reached and exactly one row when it is, with the interval configurable and defaulting to 1000

reconstructing an instance that has a snapshot at sequence S replays only events with sequence_number greater than S, and produces a state identical to the same instance reconstructed with snapshots ignored entirely -- an explicit both-paths-agree test, not just a faster-path test
the moduledoc explicitly distinguishes instance_state_snapshots (periodic execution state, this requirement) from instance_definition_snapshots (immutable PD-08 definition graph, REQ-027/REQ-033)
the moduledoc names the snapshot-cadence-counter placement as an open question left for CODE-DESIGNER, citing stage-3-instance-engine.md's second Early finding and REQ-045's process-vs-row resolution

result.summary: REWORK ITERATION 1 complete: SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4 is now wired into all four named call sites in lib/letflow/engine.ex. (1) create/2 (persist/8, ~line 211/535): new maybe_snapshot_after_create/4, piped between Repo.transaction() and interpret_create_result/5, calls maybe_take_snapshot with new_instance_state and the INSTANCE_STARTED event's own sequence_number (changes.event.sequence_number). (2) complete_task/3 (run_complete_task/6, ~line 840): new maybe_snapshot_after_complete_task/2, piped between Repo.transaction() and interpret_complete_result/1, with two clauses -- the :completed outcome uses the already-in-hand final_instance_state and the TASK_COMPLETED event's sequence_number (also covers 'on instance completion' per design doc SS4.2's 4th bullet, since final_instance_state.status is whatever the hop chain actually landed on); the {:execution_error, error_args} outcome (REQ-061, ExecutionError.append_multi/3 called at ~line 1263) reuses snapshot_and_state.seed_instance_state (accurate because the failed transition never mutated any persisted token) with status forced to :error and variables taken from error_args.variables, keyed off execution_error_event's own sequence_number. (3) set_instance_error/2 (~line 1948, ExecutionError.append_multi/3's second call site): new maybe_snapshot_after_set_instance_error/3, piped between Repo.transaction() and interpret_set_instance_error_result/3. No InstanceState is naturally in scope at this standalone entry point (it opens no Multi step that reads tokens/pending tasks) -- rather than fabricate a partial state from instance_projections.current_nodes (which would risk violating INV-ISS-1, snapshot-vs-full-replay agreement), this reuses the already-shipped, correctness-verified Letflow.Engine.Reconstruction.reconstruct_instance/2 to obtain an accurate state, accepting the O(events) cost as reasonable specifically because set_instance_error/2 is a rare, already-expensive write, not one of the two hot paths REQ-054 exists to bound. This adds a new Engine -> Reconstruction module dependency alongside Reconstruction's pre-existing Engine -> (build_graph/1, find_start_node/1, advance_until_stable/4) dependency the other way; flagged here for REVIEWER rather than silently introduced, since it completes a two-way coupling between the two modules (no compile-time/macro cycle -- both sides are plain function calls). All four sites share a private snapshot_instance/4 helper that calls SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4 and logs-and-swallows any {:error, _} via Logger.warning/1 rather than propagating it -- a SnapshotWriter failure must never turn an otherwise-successful create/2, complete_task/3, or set_instance_error/2 call into an error return, since the event log itself already durably committed and the snapshot is a read-side cache over it (SnapshotWriter's own INV-ISS-2). No public @spec of any of the three functions changed; no existing caller's pattern match on their return shapes was touched. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (both `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` targeting the 2 changed files and a full `--force` recompile of all 73 project files): clean, 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings. `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate --quiet`: no-op (this rework adds no migration -- the instance_state_snapshots migration already shipped in the prior iteration, commit 8f706a8). `mix format --check-formatted lib/letflow/engine.ex`: clean (the project-wide `mix format --check-formatted` still reports 3 pre-existing unformatted test files unrelated to this diff -- confirmed via `git status --short`, which shows only this handoff file and lib/letflow/engine.ex modified). `MIX_ENV=test mix test`: 'Finished in 124.9 seconds (5.5s async, 119.4s sync)', '5 properties, 942 tests, 0 failures' -- full suite green, including the REQ-053/REQ-044 property test and reconstruction_test.exs's both-paths-agree coverage.
issues: New Engine -> Reconstruction module dependency introduced by maybe_snapshot_after_set_instance_error/3 (calls Letflow.Engine.Reconstruction.reconstruct_instance/2), on top of Reconstruction's pre-existing Engine -> (build_graph/1, find_start_node/1, advance_until_stable/4) dependency the other way. No compile-time cycle (plain function calls, no macros), but it is a genuine two-way module coupling -- flagged for REVIEWER to confirm rather than accept by default, per this project's own rule against silently re-deciding an architectural shape.
